Hero-side: handleMarkRead-equivalent stamps localStorage dw_reading_done to today's en-CA date and calls recordStreakToday() (HomeScreen.tsx:719-723, also :787). Lesson-card side: NewBelieverLessonCard's Mark Complete button (NewBelieverLessonCard.tsx:217-231) calls savePathwayProgress, wired by HomeScreen to savePathwayProgressFromLesson (HomeScreen.tsx:4553), which itself calls savePathwayProgress(p) then, if dw_reading_done isn't already today, stamps dw_reading_done and fires the 'dw-reading-completed' event (HomeScreen.tsx:584-598). completeTodaysPathwayDay (HomeScreen.tsx:558-579) is the reverse direction: it only credits the pathway's OWN day if the hero's completed passage matches that day's assigned reading (:565-570), guards against double-completion via lastCompletedDate === today (:561) and completedDays.includes(day) (:564), then appends the day to completedDays, advances currentDay, and sets lastCompletedDay/lastCompletedDate (:571-578). The streak counter itself is HIDDEN in the UI for this persona — "Streak display — clean counter (hidden for new_to_faith + comfort to avoid pressure)" (HomeScreen.tsx:2004-2006) — even though recordStreakToday() still runs underneath it. summary: The new_to_faith Home is a single-object surface: the 40-day pathway hero card (no audio, no plans funnel, no For You, no upgrade prompt, no ads) that opens a full-screen Day N lesson+reading surface on tap. Completion is unified across the hero and the lesson card through one dw_reading_done stamp and one pathwayProgress store, with a day-matching guard so a plan reading never falsely advances the pathway. The streak still increments underneath the UI but its display is deliberately suppressed for this persona. AI is reachable only through the simplified "What this means" study-sheet action, gated by a persona-specific simple/warm system prompt; Greek/Hebrew and full highlighting stay hidden. Section visibility is driven by sectionOrder + a long tail of explicit `persona !== 'new_to_faith'` / `isNewPath` checks scattered through the 4,600-line HomeScreen.tsx, so most "self-serve" copy/flag edits are safe but any new section, gate, or completion-logic change requires a developer edit to HomeScreen.tsx directly, and any reshape of the opening screen needs Ashley's preview approval first per house rule.
